statement: In Gemma 4 E2B (35 layers, 20 KV-shared), final-position outputs depend on earlier positions only through K/V computed in layers 0-14 (stored by layers 13/14); residual states of non-final positions entering layers >=15 are causally inert for the final position.

falsification: Any nonzero change at layers >=15 under perturbation.
alternatives: Implementation detail of transformers version (e.g. cache path) differs from reference implementation

statement: Factual recall shows ROME-style early site (last subject token, middle layers) and late site (final token) under counterfactual patching.
falsification: Recovery <0.5 at all last-subject-token layers in >30% of pairs.

statement: Subject enrichment usable by later positions must be complete by layer 14 because later layers cannot read new K/V.
prediction: E004 P3; restoring only layer-13/14 K/V at subject positions recovers most of the effect.
falsification: Patching subject positions at layers 13/14 has small effect while earlier layers have large effect AND final-position late-layer patching does not explain the gap.

statement: E2B contains induction heads causally necessary for in-context copying of random token sequences.
falsification: Top-5 induction-head ablation not larger than random-5 ablations.

statement: Logit-lens answer emergence occurs in the last third of layers in Gemma 4 E2B.
alternatives: Logit lens bias in models with layer_scalar / sandwich norms

statement: Per-layer embeddings re-inject token identity at every layer, so residual-stream-only interventions underestimate token-identity effects.
prediction: Patching residual + PLE at a position recovers more than residual alone at late layers <=14.
falsification: No difference between residual-only and residual+PLE patching.
alternatives: PLE contribution small relative to residual

statement: The k/v tensors stored for KV-shared layers in the checkpoint are untrained remnants.
prediction: Their statistics match an initialization distribution and are identical or near-identical between IT and base checkpoints.
falsification: Statistics resemble trained layers or differ systematically between IT and base.
